svg.text: REFERENCE ONLY — one hold model (force_table), vendor prices on a date, a 35 % derate that is a rule of thumb. Types cannot be mixed: the magnet height is the standoff.
MAGNET ECONOMICS — hold against cost, every type, every count the plate takes
Hold = force to pull the BOTTOM edge off, plate pivoting on the fridge's top edge (the page's 'lets go at' figure). Grab case 20 lb; the dashed lines are 2x, 4x and 6x on it.
CHEAPEST WAY TO EACH TARGET (bottom-edge pull-off)
Hold is linear in count for one type: no knee inside a line. The knees are the plate's
position budget (4 corners, 4 mid-side spares already cut, 4 more with a second row pair)
Per dollar the small K&J magnets beat the O48 by 25-35 %, and eight of them fit where four
The 35 % derate is generous to thin magnets: a paint gap costs a 7 mm magnet a larger share
of its rating than an 11.5 mm one. Measure one on the panel before buying twelve.
Every K&J option is an 8 mm standoff and a 5/16 in pad, an M-thread stud and a smaller plate
hole. Pick the TYPE first (it sets the plate), then the COUNT (spares are just holes).
Twist (press the screen edge to unseat it) scales the same way and is never the limit: even 4 x MM-C-20 read 15 lb against a 5 lb press.
Sources: K&J product pages 2026-09-02; McMaster 3506K67 2026-08-27; hold model force_table.forces() on the built plate (310 body, inset 32, neck 257).
